title: Zcash targets November upgrade to make private payments up to three times faster
summary: Title: Zcash targets November upgrade to make private payments up to three times faster URL Source: https://www.coindesk.com/tech/2026/09/18/zcash-targets-november-upgrade-to-make-private-payments-up-to-three-times-faster Published Time: 2026-09-18T12:50:01.701Z Markdown Content: 1 day ago 2 min read ![Image 1: Computer, network upgrade (JESHOOTS-com/Pixabay)](https://www.coindesk.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.sanity.io%2Fimages%2Fs3y3vcno%2Fproduction%2F837700a2c31b20bd836c2e16853b6d25f4e30f7f-5400x3600.jpg%3Frect%3D0%2C281%2C5400%2C3038%26w%3D1920%26h%3D1080%26auto%3Dformat&w=3840&q=75) (JESHOOTS-com/Pixabay) Summary * Zcash developers are targeting Nov. 5 for the NU7 upgrade, which would cut block times to 25 seconds from 75 seconds and make private payments faster. * NU7 would temporarily remove about 60% of transaction fees from circulation, with the funds scheduled to return as mining rewards beginning in February 2031. * The upgrade preserves Zcash’s issuance and halving schedule by reducing rewards per block and tripling the halving interval, while its final activation decision is due Oct. 20. Zcash developers are [targeting Nov. 5 an upgrade](https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/nu7-timeline/57655) that would cut the time between blocks from 75 seconds to 25 to go live. The NU7 upgrade would also begin setting aside part of the network’s transaction fees for future mining rewards. The timetable follows talks among the core builder teams Zcash Foundation, Project Tachyon, Valar, ZODL and Shielded Labs. The groups and engineering teams reached unanimous agreement on the upgrade’s contents after a series of community and coinholder polls. About 2.4 million ZEC participated in the vote, equal to 66% of the eligible pool. Some 98.9% backed keeping Zcash’s existing halving schedule, while 96.6% chose February 2031 as the starting point for returning collected fees to miners. (Solana) Summary * Solana reduced its target slot time to 250 milliseconds from 300 milliseconds, giving applications faster network updates and potentially reducing failed or poorly priced trades. * The nearly 17 percent speed increase does not raise overall transaction capacity because each slot is permitted to carry proportionally less computation and data. * The change shortens epochs to about 30 hours and leaves less time for offline signing and delayed approvals, while a proposed reduction to 200 milliseconds has no mainnet date. Solana cut its target slot time from 300 milliseconds to 250 milliseconds earlier Friday, [blockchain data](https://explorer.solana.com/address/iBRLMc81UjRa8fn8A6eE8bJTnRbgQoPTynM51akENCV) shows, making the network’s clock run nearly 17% faster without producing an equivalent increase in total transaction capacity. A single train still carries the exact same number of people and the total number of people moving through the station per hour remains the same.
